He was 86. members.title: 'Star Trek', 'X-Men' star Patrick Stewart dead at 86
members.lead: Patrick Stewart, the British Shakespearean actor who became a Hollywood megastar through roles in the "Star Trek" and "X-Men" franchises, has died at his home in Los Angeles. He was 86. His death on Wednesday came after a "brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, according to an official statement on his social media accounts. "His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre," the statement said. The actor, who hailed from the northern English region of Yorkshire, trod the boards in Britain with the Royal Shakespeare Company and the National Theatre in London, and worked on British television. But he rocketed into the pop culture history books in his mid-40s when he was cast as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in "Star Trek: The Next Generation," and then again as Professor Charles Xavier in multiple "X-Men" and related Marvel films. .'Breaking Bad' actor RJ Mitte dead: representatives. A proud Yorkshireman, Stewart "wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and in my case, love," Ian McKellan said of his "X-Men" co-star and dear friend. McKellan, 87, recounted meeting Stewart in London and hearing about his "Star Trek" offer, warning him he may get lost in Hollywood and to think of his stage career. "Well, he took the risk and thank goodness for us all that he did." . Stewart was 47 when he debuted as Picard in "Star Trek: The Next Generation," the first live-action television spinoff of the trailblazing late-1960s sci-fi series. He effectively filled the boots of William Shatner's Captain Kirk -- to resounding success, both in the TV series and in several films. Picard became known for a few catchphrases including "Make it so" and "Engage!" But his move to America in 1987 was initially greeted with disdain by the Los Angeles Times, who wrote him off as an "unknown British Shakespearean actor." .
